edges.label: ATIC was the terminal analytical authority under the regulation
edges.note: The regulation routes reports from base level through Air Defense Command and the 4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron to ATIC at Wright-Patterson for final analysis.

edges.label: AFR 200-2 governed what Blue Book could say publicly
edges.note: For unexplainable objects, 'only the fact that ATIC will analyze the data is worthy of release'. Every Air Force public statement that unknowns were unimportant was made under a regulation forbidding discussion of them.

edges.label: The 1954 regulation was issued under Twining as Chief of Staff
edges.note: The officer who wrote in 1947 that the phenomenon was real was Air Force Chief of Staff when the regulation restricting public discussion of unexplained cases was promulgated.

edges.label: Panel recommendations became binding Air Force regulation
edges.note: AFR 200-2 was issued 26 August 1953 and revised 12 August 1954, restricting public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact of ATIC analysis — the debunking recommendation converted into internal law within months of the panel reporting.
